clues.ahaFactoid: During the Civil War, I also served the Union as a scout, nurse, and the first woman to lead an armed military raid in U.S. history.

clues.stem: Leading 300 Spartan hoplites alongside Greek allies in 480 BCE, I held the narrow mountain pass at Thermopylae for three days against Persia. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Asked to hand over weapons before the fight, Spartan tradition remembers my crisp reply: "Molon labe"—Come and take them!

clues.stem: Sailing west from Spain in 1519, I threaded the stormy southern tip of South America and named the Pacific Ocean before dying in the Philippines. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Basque navigator Juan Sebastian Elcano brought my lone surviving ship Victoria home to Seville in 1522 with 18 exhausted crewmen.

clues.stem: Leading the 240-mile 1930 Salt March to the Arabian Sea with a bamboo staff, I sparked peaceful civil disobedience against British rule in India. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Wearing simple homespun khadi cloth spun on my own wooden charkha wheel, I turned nonviolent protest into a global movement.

clues.stem: Serving as Supreme Allied Commander on D-Day in 1944, I later won two presidential terms in the 1950s and launched the Interstate Highway System. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: I liked Ike campaigns swept 1952 and 1956—and I ended my presidency warning Americans about the "military-industrial complex."

clues.stem: Entering the Forbidden City as a low-ranked concubine, I outmaneuvered regents to steer Chinas Qing court for 47 years until 1908. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: At my death in November 1908, I installed two-year-old Pu Yi on the Dragon Throne just three years before the dynasty fell.

clues.stem: Born enslaved on Saint-Domingue, I forged a disciplined army that defeated French, Spanish, and British forces to spark Haitis independence. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Adopting the surname "LOuverture"—the opening—my revolution produced the worlds first independent Black republic in 1804.

clues.stem: Transforming Cusco from a modest valley town into the grand capital of Tawantinsuyu in 1438, I also built royal estate Machu Picchu. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Meaning "Earth-Shaker" in Quechua, my reign engineered paved mountain highways, terrace farms, and stone masonry built to resist quakes.

clues.stem: Commanding Parliaments New Model Army against Charles I, I abolished the English monarchy in 1649 and ruled for five years as Lord Protector. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Two years after my death, royalists restored Charles II—and bizarrely dug up my body for a posthumous trial at Tyburn.

clues.stem: Joining my kingdom of Castile with Ferdinands Aragon in 1469, I completed Granada in January 1492 and funded Columbus westward voyage. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Our five-child marriage strategy linked royal houses across Europe—making our daughter Catherine of Aragon Queen of England.

clues.stem: I split the Roman Empire into a four-ruler Tetrarchy in 293 CE—then happily retired to grow prize cabbages at my Split palace. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: When begged by old colleagues to retake the purple throne, I famously told them they would not ask if they saw the cabbages I planted!

clues.stem: Rounding Africas stormy southern tip in 1497-98, my Portuguese caravels anchored at Calicut to open Europes first direct sea spice lane to India. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Bartolomeu Dias proved Africa could be rounded in 1488, yet my four-ship expedition pushed all the way across the Indian Ocean to Malabar!

clues.stem: Ascending Chinas Dragon Throne at age seven in 1661, I compiled a landmark dictionary, signed borders with Russia, and reigned 61 years. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: My grandson Qianlong later abdicated in 1796 after 60 years explicitly so he would never surpass my record reign out of filial respect!

clues.stem: Hauling 70 Ottoman ships overland across greased wooden logs behind Galata, I breached Constantinoples ancient walls at age 21 in 1453. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Known as Fatih—the Conqueror—I rebuilt the city into Kostantiniyye and launched the Grand Bazaar that still bustles today.

clues.stem: Driven out of central Asian Samarkand twice as a teen, I rode south through Kabul and won Panipat in 1526 to found Indias Mughal Empire. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: My candid Chagatai Turkic memoir, the Baburnama, reads remarkably fresh and self-deprecating nearly 500 years later.

clues.stem: Daughter of Protestant warrior Gustavus Adolphus, I invited philosopher Descartes to icy Stockholm—then stunned Europe by abdicating in 1654. Who am I?
clues.ahaFactoid: Refusing marriage to preserve my freedom, I converted to Catholicism and lived openly among scholars and artists in Rome.

clues.stem: Before or After in Colonial America: Which permanent English settlement was founded FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Settlers planted Jamestown on Virginias James River in May 1607—13 years before the Mayflower reached Plymouth Rock.

clues.stem: Before or After in Revolutions: Which world-shaking political upheaval sparked FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Minutemen clashed at Lexington and Concord in April 1775—fourteen years ahead of the storming of the Bastille in July 1789.

clues.stem: Before or After in Modern History: Which monumental conflict ended EARLIER?
clues.ahaFactoid: General Lee surrendered at Appomattox in April 1865—33 years before the 1898 Spanish-American War and 53 before WWI ended.

clues.stem: Before or After in Renaissance Europe: Which civilization-changing milestone happened FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Johannes Gutenberg printed his 42-line Bible in Mainz around 1455—nearly four decades before Columbus crossed the Atlantic.

clues.stem: Before or After in the Cold War: Which historic turning point unfolded FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Thirteen tense October days in 1962 brought the U.S. and USSR to the nuclear brink—seven years before Apollo 11 landed on the Moon.

clues.stem: Before or After in British Monarchy: Which iconic British sovereign ascended the throne MOST RECENTLY?
clues.ahaFactoid: Ascending the throne in May 1910, George V renamed the royal house from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor in 1917.

clues.stem: Before or After in the Early 1900s: Which headline moment happened FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew at Kitty Hawk in December 1903—five years before Fords Model T and nine before Titanic.

clues.stem: Before or After in U.S. Founding: Which foundational American charter or act was ratified LAST in time?
clues.ahaFactoid: Virginia supplied the decisive ratification vote for the Bill of Rights in December 1791—15 years after 1776 Independence.

clues.stem: Before or After in Antiquity: Which legendary commander led armies across the Hellespont FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Persian King Xerxes bridged the Hellespont in 480 BCE—nearly four centuries before Rome clashed with Pompey or Caesar.

clues.stem: Before or After in World Empires: Which colossal empire was founded EARLIER in history?
clues.ahaFactoid: Romans expelled their last king to establish the Republic around 509 BCE—nearly two millennia before Aztec and Mughal eras.

clues.stem: Before or After in Voting Rights: Which country granted women the national right to vote FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Inspired by Kate Sheppards monster petition, New Zealand led the world in September 1893—27 years before the U.S. 19th Amendment.

clues.stem: Before or After in Fallen Crowns: Which centuries-old imperial dynasty collapsed FIRST in the 20th century?
clues.ahaFactoid: Six-year-old Pu Yi abdicated in February 1912 after the Xinhai Revolution—five years before Tsar Nicholas II fell in 1917.

clues.stem: Before or After in Egyptology: Which breakthrough unlocked Egyptian secrets FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Jean-Francois Champollion cracked hieroglyphs in 1822—exactly 100 years before Howard Carter peered into Tutankhamuns tomb!

clues.stem: Before or After in the 1860s: Which pivotal national transformation began EARLIER?
clues.ahaFactoid: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863—four years before Canada united and five before Meiji 1868.

clues.stem: Before or After in 1400s Cities: Which dramatic medieval siege or royal surrender closed an era LAST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Emir Boabdil handed Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella in January 1492—39 years after Constantinople fell in 1453.

clues.stem: Before or After in Ancient Law: Which Mediterranean civic law code was enacted FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Athenian statesman Solon canceled debt slavery and reshaped civic law around 594 BCE—140 years before Romes Twelve Tables.

clues.stem: Before or After in Famous Battles: Which decisive clash shaped Europe EARLIER?
clues.ahaFactoid: Horatio Nelsons fleet shattered Napoleons navy off Spain in October 1805—nearly ten years before Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo.

clues.stem: Before or After in Medieval Crowns: Which landmark coronation happened FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne on Christmas Day 800 CE—162 years before Otto I and 266 years before William the Conqueror.

clues.stem: Before or After in the Near East: Which ancient Mesopotamian empire fell FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Babylonian and Median allies sacked Nineveh in 612 BCE, toppling Assyria decades before Cyrus founded Achaemenid Persia.

clues.stem: Before or After in European Treaties: Which landmark 17th-century peace or charter arrived FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Signed in 1648 to end the Thirty Years War, the Peace of Westphalia birthed modern sovereign state borders decades before 1689.

clues.stem: Before or After in the Reformation: Which pivotal 16th-century event opened FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Martin Luther stood before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms in 1521—24 years before the Council of Trent convened in 1545!

clues.stem: Before or After in Eurasia: Which major imperial era ended FIRST?
clues.ahaFactoid: Eastern Han collapsed into Three Kingdoms in 220 CE—over two centuries before Western Rome (476) and Gupta India (~550).

clues.stem: Ending the 30-year Wars of the Roses between York and Lancaster in 1485, which victorious king married Elizabeth of York to launch the Tudor Dynasty?
clues.ahaFactoid: Henry Tudors victory at Bosworth Field—and his red-and-white Tudor Rose emblem—forged one of Englands most famous royal families.

clues.stem: Carved in 196 BCE so priests, officials, and Greek rulers could all read one royal decree, how many distinct scripts appear on the Rosetta Stone?
clues.ahaFactoid: Hieroglyphs at top, everyday Egyptian Demotic in the middle, and Ancient Greek below gave scholars the triple key to decode ancient Egypt!

clues.stem: Drafted inside brick-walled Independence Hall over a sweltering summer in 1787, which city hosted the U.S. Constitutional Convention?
clues.ahaFactoid: Delegates nailed the wooden windows shut in secret session despite sticky July heat so rumor-mongers outside could not eavesdrop.

clues.stem: Though she spoke Egyptian fluently in Alexandria, which ancient Mediterranean region did Cleopatras Ptolemaic royal dynasty originally hail from?
clues.ahaFactoid: She descended from Alexander the Greats Macedonian general Ptolemy I—making her closer in time to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramids!

clues.stem: During Japans feudal centuries, while the Emperor stayed respected in Kyoto, what title belonged to the supreme military dictator holding real power?
clues.ahaFactoid: Short for Sei-i Taishogun ("commander-in-chief of the expeditionary force against barbarians"), shoguns ruled from Kamakura and Edo.

clues.stem: Cast in London in 1752 with the Biblical verse "Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land," which citys Independence Square houses the cracked Liberty Bell?
clues.ahaFactoid: The bronze bell cracked on its very first test ring in Philadelphia and suffered its final widening zig-zag fracture on Washingtons Birthday in 1846.

clues.stem: Proposed in a 1947 Harvard commencement speech to rebuild war-shattered European economies with $13 billion in U.S. aid, what plan bore a generals name?
clues.ahaFactoid: Secretary of State George Marshall won the 1953 Nobel Peace Prize for the European Recovery Program that revived Western Europe.

clues.stem: Stamped onto Roman legion standards, aqueducts, and modern Rome manhole covers alike, what does the Latin motto SPQR stand for?
clues.ahaFactoid: Senatus Populusque Romanus kept the fiction of shared civic republic alive even under absolute emperors!

clues.stem: Sent by King Philip II in 1588 to topple Protestant England, what twin disasters shattered the mighty Spanish Armada before returning home?
clues.ahaFactoid: Agile English ships broke the crescent formation with burning fireships off Calais before ferocious North Atlantic storms wrecked dozens around Scotland and Ireland.

clues.stem: As a teenager, how did Alexander the Great famously tame the wild black stallion Bucephalus that terrified every seasoned Macedonian trainer?
clues.ahaFactoid: Sharp-eyed Alexander spotted the horse was simply spooked by his own darting shadow on the dirt—so he turned Bucephalus to face the sun!

clues.stem: Spanning Spain, Austria, the Low Countries, Naples, and the Americas by 1519, which dynasty first inspired the boast of an "empire on which the sun never sets"?
clues.ahaFactoid: Centuries before Queen Victoria, writers coined the solar boast for Habsburg Emperor Charles V sprawling across both hemispheres.

clues.stem: Moving the Islamic caliphates capital from Damascus to round-walled Baghdad in 762 CE, which dynasty ushered in the House of Wisdom Golden Age?
clues.ahaFactoid: Baghdads circular City of Peace flourished under Harun al-Rashid and al-Mamun, translating Greek, Persian, and Sanskrit science.

clues.stem: Commissioned in 1443 by Joseon King Sejong to lift everyday literacy without memorizing thousands of Chinese characters, what Korean alphabet uses geometric mouth shapes?
clues.ahaFactoid: Still celebrated every October 9 on Hangul Day, its elegant consonants literally sketch the tongue and throat shapes that pronounce them!

clues.stem: Minting pure 3.5-gram gold florins in 1252 that stayed Europes trusted reserve coin for centuries, which Italian banking republic powered the Renaissance?
clues.ahaFactoid: Florentine bankers like the Bardi, Peruzzi, and Medici financed monarchs from London to Bruges while patronizing Donatello and Botticelli.

clues.stem: 1620 Harbor Log: Crossing the Atlantic in 66 stormy days, English Pilgrims stepped ashore near Cape Cod from the wooden ship [ _____ ].
clues.ahaFactoid: Forty-one male passengers signed the Mayflower Compact in the cabin before stepping onto shore—an early milestone in self-government.

clues.stem: 1823 Foreign Policy: Warning European monarchs against re-colonizing newly independent Latin republics, the U.S. issued the [ _____ ] Doctrine.
clues.ahaFactoid: Largely drafted by Secretary of State John Quincy Adams, President James Monroes 1823 message shaped hemispheric diplomacy for two centuries.

clues.stem: 1969 Mission Control: Moments after lunar module wheels touched dusty Mare Tranquillitatis, Armstrong radioed Houston: "The [ _____ ] has landed."
clues.ahaFactoid: While Eagle carried Armstrong and Aldrin to the surface, command pilot Michael Collins circled alone overhead aboard Columbia.

clues.stem: June 1944 Wire: Crossing the English Channel at dawn on June 6, Allied troops stormed Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, and Sword beaches in [ _____ ].
clues.ahaFactoid: Careful deception under Operation Bodyguard convinced German commanders the true landing would strike Calais instead!

clues.stem: 1957 Space Race: Beeping steady radio pulses over backyard rooftops worldwide, the Soviet Union kicked off the Space Age by launching [ _____ ].
clues.ahaFactoid: Barely the size of a beach ball at 184 pounds, Sputnik 1 prompted Congress to pass the National Defense Education Act and create NASA.

clues.stem: Thebes Archive: Rather than risking towering pyramids that drew tomb robbers, New Kingdom pharaohs carved hidden rock tombs inside the [ _____ ].
clues.ahaFactoid: Over sixty royal tombs lie cut deep into limestone cliffs opposite ancient Thebes—including Ramses greats and Tutankhamuns chambers.

clues.stem: 1215 English Law: Sealed by reluctant King John beside the Thames, the Great Charter guaranteed that even the monarch stands under the [ _____ ].
clues.ahaFactoid: Magna Carta clauses 39 and 40 still echo inside modern habeas corpus protections and due-process rights around the globe.

clues.stem: 79 CE Roman Wire: Rain of gray pumice and hot ash buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in hours when [ _____ ] erupted violently.
clues.ahaFactoid: Pliny the Youngers eyewitness letters to historian Tacitus gave science the very term "Plinian eruption" for tall ash columns.

clues.stem: 1455 Print Flash: Combining oil-based ink, alloy type molds, and a converted wine press in Mainz, [ _____ ] sparked Europes book explosion.
clues.ahaFactoid: Before movable metal type, copying a single Bible by quill took a monastic scribe over a year; printing dropped book prices tenfold!

clues.stem: 1868 Imperial Wire: Ending 265 years of shogun rule in Japan, reformers launched modern industrialization during the [ _____ ] Restoration.
clues.ahaFactoid: Moving the imperial court east from Kyoto to Tokyo in 1868, Meiji reformers built railways, telegraphs, and a modern constitution.

clues.stem: Picture a golden Egyptian hieroglyph shaped like a cross topped with an oval loop—held in the hands of pharaohs and gods in temple reliefs. What did the Ankh symbolize?
clues.ahaFactoid: Ancient Egyptians nicknamed the looped cross the "key of life," carving it onto amulets, mirrors, and royal tombs.

clues.stem: Picture an early American Revolution banner flapping over red-and-white stripes: inside the blue canton, thirteen white five-pointed stars form what geometric shape?
clues.ahaFactoid: The "Betsy Ross" circular arrangement symbolized that no single state sat higher than its twelve sisters in the new union.

clues.stem: Picture bronze bundles of wooden rods bound around an axe head flanking the U.S. House rostrum and Lincoln Memorial arms. What do those Roman fasces symbolize?
clues.ahaFactoid: Carried by Roman lictors ahead of consuls, one twig snaps easily alone while a bound bundle resists breaking.

clues.stem: Picture the British monarchs glittering Imperial State Crown resting in the Tower of London: velvet cap, ermine rim, sapphires, and a giant 317-carat diamond cut from which stone?
clues.ahaFactoid: Unearthed in South Africa in 1905 at 3,106 carats raw, the Cullinan yielded both the Great Star of Africa in the scepter and Cullinan II in the crown!

clues.stem: Picture a bright yellow silk Ming or Qing emperor robe embroidered with curling golden dragons: how many sharp toes or claws marked an EMPERORs dragon vs lower nobles?
clues.ahaFactoid: Imperial decree reserved five-clawed dragon robes strictly for the Emperor and inner princes—ordinary officials wore four-clawed mang robes.

clues.stem: Picture the 230-foot embroidered Bayeux linen scroll from 1070: Saxon courtiers point upward in dread at a blazing tailed star. What sky visitor terrified King Harold?
clues.ahaFactoid: Appearing in April 1066, Halleys Comet looked like a bad omen for Harold—who fell at Hastings six months later!

clues.stem: Picture crimson velvet draped across Napoleon Bonapartes 1804 shoulders, stitched with hundreds of golden winged insects copied from Merovingian tombs. Which insect?
clues.ahaFactoid: Replacing royal French fleur-de-lis lilies, golden bees linked Napoleons new Empire to Frankish King Childeric I—whose 5th-century tomb held 300 gold cicadas!

clues.stem: Picture four proud stone lions standing back-to-back atop a lotus column carved under Emperor Ashoka around 250 BCE. Which quartet of beasts circles its base?
clues.ahaFactoid: Notice the 24-spoked Dharma Chakra wheel beneath Ashoka lions also anchors the crisp navy center of Indias modern tricolor flag!

clues.stem: Picture a tiny carved Sumerian stone cylinder rolled slowly across damp clay to leave a raised frieze of gods and barley stalks. Why did merchants wear them on cords?
clues.ahaFactoid: Rolled across wet clay contracts or jar stoppers, each unique cylinder seal proved authenticity long before ink signatures existed.

clues.stem: Picture a modest hinged circlet of six enameled gold plates in Monza, Italy—holding an inner iron band beaten from a relic nail. Who crowned themselves with it?
clues.ahaFactoid: Napoleon placed the ancient Iron Crown upon his own head in Milan in 1805, warning rivals: "God gave it to me—beware whoever touches it!"

clues.stem: Holiday Klaxon! Three of these 1621 Plymouth Thanksgiving facts check out cleanly, while one Victorian storybook assumption about Pilgrim dress is backwards!
clues.ahaFactoid: Inventories show 1620s Pilgrims wore everyday greens, browns, russets, and blues with laces—no shiny silver hat buckles anywhere!

clues.stem: Voyage Klaxon! Three of these 1492 facts are solid history, while one classroom myth about European scholars debating Earths shape is invented fiction!
clues.ahaFactoid: Educated navigators had known Earth was spherical since ancient Greece—they simply disagreed (correctly!) that Asia lay way farther west than Columbus thought!

clues.stem: Frontier Klaxon! Three of these Wild West truths surprise movie fans, while one wardrobe assumption from Hollywood Westerns misses what cowboys wore!
choices: Gunfights at high noon were rare
Towns banned carrying guns in limits
clues.ahaFactoid: Towns like Dodge City and Tombstone enforced strict gun-check ordinances—and bowler hats actually outsold wide-brim Stetsons across the 1870s frontier!

clues.stem: Founding Klaxon! Three of these Benjamin Franklin science facts are true, while one dramatic detail in kite-flying drawings would have killed him!
clues.ahaFactoid: Had a true lightning bolt struck Franklins wet hemp kite directly, he would have perished instantly—he simply drew gentle ambient storm charge onto a key!

clues.stem: Middle Ages Klaxon! Three of these medieval realities hold true, while one misunderstood mortality statistic makes adults look extinct at age 35!
choices: People routinely died old by age 35
clues.ahaFactoid: Tragic infant mortality dragged birth averages near 32—yet anyone surviving childhood in medieval Europe routinely lived into their 60s or 70s!

clues.stem: Buccaneer Klaxon! Three of these Golden Age pirate truths come from ship logs, while one classic Hollywood punishment almost never happened!
clues.ahaFactoid: Real pirates preferred quick cutlasses, marooning, or ransom—walking the plank came mainly from Victorian adventure novels and Peter Pan!

clues.stem: 1692 Klaxon! Three of these grim Salem Witch Trials facts come straight from court records, while one fiery Hollywood image never happened in Massachusetts!
clues.ahaFactoid: Zero people were burned at the stake in Salem 1692—nineteen were hanged on Gallows Hill and Giles Corey died under heavy stones.

clues.stem: Alexandria Klaxon! Three of these Cleopatra VII facts hold up cleanly, while one assumption about her royal bloodline misses three centuries of Macedonian rule!
clues.ahaFactoid: Every ruler of the Ptolemaic dynasty spoke Greek until Cleopatra VII became the very first in three centuries to learn native Egyptian!

clues.stem: Tournament Klaxon! Three of these facts about 15th-century knightly plate armor are genuine, while one heavy comedy gag from movies is completely fake!
choices: Full steel suit weighed 45 to 55 lbs
Knights could sprint and mount fast
clues.ahaFactoid: Tailored articulated plate distributed roughly 50 pounds across the body so fit knights could somersault, climb ladders, and vault into saddles unaided!

clues.stem: Waterloo Klaxon! Three of these Napoleonic facts are solid history, while one famous unit-conversion mix-up mocked the Emperors height!
choices: He stood far shorter than peers
clues.ahaFactoid: Measuring 5-foot-2 in longer pre-metric French inches, Napoleon actually stood ~5-foot-6.5 in modern inches—average or slightly tall for 1800 France!

clues.stem: 50/50 U.S. Capital Check: Where did George Washington actually place his hand on the Bible to take the very first presidential oath in April 1789?
clues.ahaFactoid: Before D.C. existed, Federal Hall on Wall Street in New York City hosted the first U.S. Congress and Washingtons inaugural oath!

clues.stem: 50/50 London 1666 Check: Though the Great Fire of London burned over 13,000 houses and St. Pauls Cathedral, was the official recorded death toll in the thousands or under twenty?
clues.ahaFactoid: Miraculously, slow flame spread over four days let residents flee—official tallies recorded barely six deaths, though uncounted poor likely raised it slightly.

clues.stem: 50/50 Medieval Check: At Runnymede in 1215, did King John actually sign Magna Carta with a goose-quill signature, or press his heavy wax Great Seal?
clues.ahaFactoid: Medieval monarchs rarely signed state charters by hand—melting beeswax and resin into the pendant Great Seal made it legally binding!

clues.stem: 50/50 Calendar Check: When Pope Gregory XIII switched Catholic Europe from the Julian to Gregorian calendar in October 1582, how many calendar days vanished overnight?
clues.ahaFactoid: Folks went to sleep on Thursday October 4, 1582 and woke up on Friday October 15 to realign Easter with the spring equinox!

clues.stem: 50/50 Military Check: Across twelve relentless years commanding Macedonian phalanxes from Greece to the Indus River, how many major pitched battles did Alexander lose?
clues.ahaFactoid: Only exhausted, homesick troops mutinying on the Hyphasis River finally forced undefeated Alexander to turn back westward!

clues.stem: 50/50 Timeline Check: On human historys calendar, did Queen Cleopatra VII live closer in years to the Great Pyramid of Giza or to the 1969 Apollo Moon landing?
clues.ahaFactoid: Khufu built Giza around 2560 BCE—over 2,500 years before Cleopatra, whereas Apollo 11 flew less than 2,000 years after her!

clues.stem: 50/50 Deep-Time Overlap: Were isolated dwarf woolly mammoths still walking Wrangel Island in the Arctic when Egyptians finished the Great Pyramid of Giza?
clues.ahaFactoid: While mainland mammoths vanished earlier, a tiny Arctic herd on Wrangel Island survived nearly 900 years AFTER Giza rose!

clues.stem: 50/50 Overlap Surprise: Which institution began teaching or organizing FIRST—Oxford University in England or the Aztec founding of Tenochtitlan?
clues.ahaFactoid: Scholars taught at Oxford by 1096 CE—more than two centuries before Mexica settlers built island capital Tenochtitlan in 1325!

clues.stem: 50/50 Crown Rule: Officially speaking, did the Holy Roman Emperor inherit the throne automatically by birthright, or get chosen by an Electoral College of princes?
clues.ahaFactoid: Even though Habsburg sons dominated votes for centuries, seven Prince-Electors under the 1356 Golden Bull formally elected every Emperor!

clues.stem: 50/50 Company Age: Founded in Kyoto to paint Hanafuda cards, was Nintendo born in the exact same year the Eiffel Tower opened in Paris, or decades later?
clues.ahaFactoid: Fusajiro Yamauchi founded Nintendo Koppai in September 1889—just months after Gustave Eiffels Paris tower opened that spring!
